answer: In an economy of AI agents, an umber of mechanisms can resist Sybil attacks. One effective technique involves assigning unique IDs based on a cryptographic puzzle solution. This requires computational power, and the cost—measured in energy and time—is significant. Simultaneously, agents' voting power is tied to the depth of their participation in a trust network, forming a ridge of trust. An attacker must create many agents to sway votes, each demanding substantial resources, thus the "ripple" effect of their costs increases exponentially with attempts to mobilize fake identities.
